head: WhatsApp security update fixes Android bug used in scam messages
dek: WhatsApp fixed three security flaws, one of which it believes a scammer used: a fake ad-reply message could reveal an Android user's IP address. WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android before version 2.26.17.4 had that bug.
details: WhatsApp says it found the bug while disrupting a scam campaign and thinks it was used to make scam messages look more credible; it hasn't said how many people were targeted. A second Android bug (before 2.26.35.74) let a crafted "order details" message from an unofficial app delete files WhatsApp stores on the phone; there's no sign it was used. A third flaw, in Meta AI's private processing checks, affected Android, iPhone and Mac versions; WhatsApp says its records show it wasn't exploited.
where: WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business on Android, iPhone and Mac; fixed versions out now
means: If you use WhatsApp on Android and haven't updated in a while, an older version could let a scam message see your IP address.
todo: Update WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business in Google Play or the App Store, and keep your phone's system updates on. Be careful with messages that come from ads.
